units.translation: like ἐπίφορος [carrying toward], properly said of wind, which the Latins call ferens or secundus, on which see Thes. vol. 8 p. 1018, improperly of mental faculty Aeschylus used it

Thus I corrected what is in M παῖς ὁ Μαίας ἐπιφορώτατος, πρᾶξιν [the son of Maia, most carrying, action] etc., with Erfurdt leading the way, who had corrected παῖς ὁ Μαίας ἐπεὶ φορώτατος πρᾶξιν οὐρίαν θέλων [the son of Maia, since most carrying, wishing a fair action]. The scholiast interprets as if said of wind, instead of ὁ λογικώτατος [the most rational]. Thus ἀνεμόεν φρόνημα [windy thought] is attributed to humans by Sophocles Antig. 353.
